reasons: The validators are clear and reject inconsistent input.
No test is visible in the packet, so the ordering and validation behaviour is unverified.
The docstrings warn that model_copy can bypass validation, and that is not guarded here.

terms.meaning: The most independent action a rule allows a system to take without a human deciding.
The strictest autonomy limit across all constraints, which governs the whole process.
The named regulation, standard or contract that imposes a constraint, so someone can read it.
A Python library that checks that data has the right shape and types when it is created.
Set so that an object cannot be changed after it is created.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and imports
sections.what: Explains why this module exists and imports the tools used to define typed records and validators. A reader sees no direct output from this part.
sections.why: The docstring explains that the autonomy limit is typed so it cannot be argued into a permissive value.

sections.name: ConstraintKind
sections.title: Kinds of constraint
sections.what: Lists the five kinds of thing that can limit a process: regulatory, contractual, data residency, safety and labour. Each kind has a different owner who can change it.
sections.why: The docstring says regulatory and contractual limits need different people to renegotiate them, so they must not be merged.
sections.watch_out: Merging two kinds into one sends a constraint to the wrong team.

sections.name: AutonomyCeiling (part 1)
sections.title: Autonomy levels and their order
sections.what: Defines four autonomy levels, from full autonomy to human only, and sets comparison rules so that the stricter level is always recognised as stricter. Comparisons are made by severity number, not by spelling.
sections.why: The docstring says alphabetical order inverts one pair, so comparing by text could pick the more permissive level and silently widen autonomy.
sections.watch_out: Any comparison of these levels must go through the severity order. Plain string comparison will give wrong answers.

sections.name: AutonomyCeiling: strictest
sections.title: Choosing the strictest level
sections.what: Given a set of autonomy levels, returns the strictest one. If the set is empty, it returns full autonomy, which means nothing was found that restricts the process.
sections.why: The docstring says an empty set means no constraint was recorded, not that none exists, so the evidence field is what tells the two apart.
sections.watch_out: An empty result looks the same whether no constraints were investigated or none were found. Check the evidence before trusting it.

sections.name: Constraint
sections.title: A single named constraint
sections.what: Holds one constraint with its kind, instrument name, jurisdiction, requirement, autonomy ceiling, affected steps and evidence. The record cannot be changed after creation, and it rejects unknown fields.
sections.why: The docstring says a constraint must name its instrument so a reader can look it up, because a vague statement cannot be checked or renegotiated.
sections.watch_out: Evidence identifiers are required. An empty list is allowed but marks the constraint as an unsupported hypothesis.

sections.name: DataReadiness
sections.title: Data readiness check
sections.what: Records which datasets a redesigned process needs, which are reachable today, and which have an owner and permitted access. It checks that the reachable datasets are a subset of those needed, and that governed datasets are a subset of reachable ones, and it computes the share that is usable.
sections.why: The docstring says data that exists somewhere in the organisation is not the same as data this process can reach, so availability is defined narrowly.
sections.watch_out: The readiness ratio returns 1.0 when no datasets are required, which can make an unexamined process look fully ready.

sections.name: FeasibilityAssessment
sections.title: Whole feasibility assessment
sections.what: Bundles the constraints, data readiness, binding ceiling and evidence into one frozen record. A validator recalculates the binding ceiling and rejects a stated value that disagrees. The blocking_constraints property lists the constraints that set that ceiling.
sections.why: The docstring says the ceiling is computed rather than stated, because a stated value could be permissive while a restrictive constraint sits beside it.
sections.watch_out: The constraints are stored as a tuple so they cannot be appended after creation. Replacing the record with model_copy skips the check.

summary: Defines what the constraints on a process permit and how ready its data is, with the strictest autonomy limit computed automatically.
purpose: Stops a design from proposing autonomous operation where a regulation, contract, data rule, safety rule or labour rule requires a named person to decide.
why: The module docstring says a wrongly permissive design is the most damaging failure in the system, because it looks plausible and is found only in an audit. Typed, ordered values are used so that no reader has to interpret prose.
how: First, each named constraint is recorded with its instrument, jurisdiction, requirement, permitted autonomy level and evidence. Second, the autonomy levels are ordered by severity rather than alphabetically. Third, the binding ceiling is the strictest level across all constraints, and a validator rejects any stated ceiling that differs from the computed one. Fourth, data readiness is recorded as required, available and governed datasets, with a ratio of usable datasets. Finally, the assessment bundles constraints, data readiness, the binding ceiling and evidence.
inputs: A list of constraints, each with a kind, instrument name, jurisdiction, requirement, autonomy ceiling, affected step numbers and evidence identifiers. Also a data readiness record and an evidence list.
outputs: A frozen assessment object. Its blocking_constraints property returns the constraints that set the binding ceiling, and readiness_ratio returns the share of required datasets that are both available and governed.
risks: The binding ceiling is only as correct as the constraints recorded. An empty constraint list means full autonomy is the default, so an uninvestigated process looks the same as one with no constraints. Pydantic model_copy can bypass the validator, which the docstring warns about.
debug: If a ceiling looks too permissive, check the constraint list first and confirm the strictest level is present. If a validation error mentions the binding ceiling, the stated value disagrees with the computed one. If a data readiness error appears, check that available datasets appear in required and governed datasets appear in available. Look for model_copy calls that skip validation.
